ko-news-notices-343-8372c75064.title: [New Maritime Era] Rapid development in advanced maritime countries
ko-news-notices-343-8372c75064.text:
[New Maritime Era] Rapid development in advanced maritime countries
2022-03-02
It was 33 years ago that the resource value of deep ocean water became known to the world. When the oil shock broke out in 1973, the following year, the United States, which was looking for alternative energy to replace oil, began researching ‘ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC)’, which extracts cold deep ocean water and uses the temperature difference with warm surface water to generate electricity, and the secrets of deep ocean water began to be revealed one by one.
The United States immediately established a natural energy research center in Hawaii and began industrializing deep ocean water, focusing on agriculture, fishing, alternative energy, food, and medicine. Currently, 29 food and pharmaceutical venture companies are housed in this research institute, creating employment for 200 people and generating an income of $30 million annually.
It was Japan that established the concept of developing deep ocean water commercialization technology. Japan, which began researching deep water in 1976, succeeded in developing ‘drinking water’ using deep water for the first time in 1989, forming a significant industry.
In fact, deep water development projects are underway in 18 local governments, including Kochi Prefecture, and as many as 1,000 types of deep water-related products, including bottled water, beer, beverages, salt, cosmetics, and food, are being produced. The market size reaches 2.5 trillion won per year. Drinking water made from deep ocean water in Japan is imported into Korea as a mixed drink and sold at very high prices in department stores.
Norway is using deep water for salmon farming, and Taiwan has also been working on industrialization, including marketing bottled water using deep water since last year.
Reporter Ahn Kyung-ho (Hankook Ilbo, khan@hk.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-344-8372c75064.title: [Saemangeum land-use plan finalized after 20 years] 70% of reclaimed land designated as farmland
ko-news-notices-344-8372c75064.text:
[Saemangeum use plan confirmed after 20 years] 70% of reclaimed land is farmland
2022-03-02
The 'Land Use Plan' for the Saemangeum reclamation project, which began as an election pledge by then Democratic Justice Party candidate Roh Tae-woo during the 1987 presidential election, was finally finalized after 20 years.
The plan is to focus on developing Buan-gun, which is close to Byeonsan National Park, by 2020, and to build foreign direct investment (FDI) areas and logistics facilities in Gunsan-si from 2020 to 2030.
This plan is different from the idea that local governments such as Jeollabuk-do have been advocating for ‘distributed development’, where industrial complexes, new towns, and tourist sites are located in adjacent areas of Gunsan, Gimje, and Buan-gun.
A government official said, "Of the land classified as agricultural land, 41.5㎢ (12.55 million pyeong) has been classified as reserved land so that it can be converted to other uses, so it may be readjusted in the future if additional leisure facilities such as golf courses or industrial complexes are needed."
◆Some farmland can be converted to use
The Saemangeum reclamation project has a total area of 401㎢ (121.3 million pyeong), which is 140 times the size of Yeouido in Seoul and two-thirds of the size of Seoul.
Among these, the internal reclamation area, excluding the 118㎢ (35.7 million pyeong) created as a freshwater lake, is 283㎢ (85.8 million pyeong), which is 100 times the area of ​​Yeouido.
Construction of the Saemangeum project began in 1991, but construction was halted for two years and five months starting in 1999 due to the contamination of Sihwa Lake and lawsuits filed by environmental groups.
The government prioritized ‘securing high-quality farmland’ as the development principle for Saemangeum reclaimed land.
It was decided to develop land (61.25 million pyeong) equivalent to 71.6% of the Saemangeum reclaimed area into rice fields and a horticultural complex.
It is important to secure high-quality farmland as it is expected that 1.288 billion pyeong (4,260 ㎢) of the total agricultural land in Korea (18.36 billion pyeong, as of 2005) will decrease by 2030.
However, the government classified 12.5 million pyeong of Saemangeum farmland as 'reserved land' and initially used it as rice paddies for rental farming, allowing it to be converted to use later.
For example, the FDI area to be created after 2030 is planned to be created by diverting 4.2 million pyeong of farmland classified as reserved farmland.
The article also anticipated that if demand for golf courses and other facilities increased, some farmland would be converted to other uses, potentially reducing farmland in Saemangeum to 56% of the total reclaimed area.
◆Gunsan for industry, Buan for tourism
The government applied ‘selection and concentration’ as the Saemangeum development principle.
In order to maximize the effect of connection with the Gunjang district, an industrial complex area, it was decided to concentrate industrial sites, foreign investment zones, and logistics facilities in areas adjacent to Gunsan City.
The plan is to first create an industrial complex area of ​​2.8 million pyeong by 2020, and then complete the remainder by 2030, when seawater distribution ends.
It was decided to attract companies related to the automobile, petrochemical, biological and biotechnology industries to the Saemangeum Industrial Complex.
It was decided to concentrate the tourist attractions in the southern area of ​​Saemangeum (Buan-gun) so that they can be developed in connection with Byeonsan Peninsula National Park.
2.4 million pyeong will be allocated to build 8 golf courses (based on 18 holes), and the rest will be used for marine entertainment facilities such as water parks and marina facilities, a wellness complex, hotels, and holiday lodgings.
The government estimates that tourism demand for Saemangeum and surrounding areas will reach 11.51 million people per year in 2020.
◆"No new city construction"
The government decided not to build a separate new city in the Saemangeum area.
The government's position is that workers in the industrial complexes can be accommodated in the 'Gunsan urbanization area' and that population growth generated by increased foreign direct investment can be accommodated by developing areas around Gunsan City.
As a result, Jeollabuk-do's plan to create a new city, such as an enterprise city, in the hinterland of Gimje City was in vain.
Jeollabuk-do has been requesting that land use plans be drawn up in the following areas: 'Gunsan-Industrial Complex', 'Gimje-Foreign Investment Zone/Enterprise City Construction', and 'Buan-Tourism Complex' in the sense of 'dispersed deployment for balanced regional development'.
The concentrated placement of golf courses and leisure complexes in Buan-gun could also be a factor in causing conflict within the region.
In the case of industrial land, some are claiming that it is unrealistic to create an additional 5.65 million pyeong (18.7㎢) at a time when the occupancy rate of the Gunjang Industrial Complex near Saemangeum is only 30%.
Reporter Hyun Seung-yoon/Kim Hong-yeol hyunsy@hankyung.com

ko-news-notices-345-8372c75064.title: A 770,000-pyeong new ocean city will be created in Masan by filling in the sea by 2017.
ko-news-notices-345-8372c75064.text:
A 770,000-pyeong new ocean city will be created in Masan by filling in the sea by 2017.
2022-03-02
A marine city measuring 770,000 pyeong will be built in the West Port district of Masan-si, Gyeongsangnam-do and the Gapo district, the hinterland of Masan New Port, by 2017.
Masan City, Gyeongsangnam-do, decided to promote Masan Marine City, which will reclaim the sea in the area and create a new city, as an urban development method, and held an inaugural general meeting of Masan Marine City Co., Ltd., which is composed of the city and private operators such as Hyundai Development Company, Sammi Construction, Daekyung Construction, Geonil Engineering, and Kookmin Bank on the 21st.
Masan Marine City Co., Ltd. has a founding capital of 1 billion won, and Hyundai Development Company (29.5%) and Masan City (28.5%) own more than half of the shares.
This project will invest KRW 691 billion to create 770,000 pyeong of land through marine reclamation and other methods to be used as residential and commercial land.
Masan Marine City Co., Ltd. will act on behalf of Masan City for 10 years until the project is completed in 2017, and will be in charge of tasks such as financing and ordering various impact assessment services, various compensation surveys and data preparation in the West Port and Gapo districts, and establishment and distribution of sales plans.
Masan Marine New Town Co., Ltd. will hold a financial agreement signing ceremony for a loan of 150 billion won at the Masan Savoy Hotel at 11:30 a.m. on the 26th with five lenders, including Kookmin Bank, National Nonghyup Bank, Kyongnam Bank, Busan Bank, and Suhyup Bank, attending.

ko-news-notices-346-8372c75064.title: The chart near Gunsan Port changes.
ko-news-notices-346-8372c75064.text:
The chart near Gunsan Port changes.
2022-03-02
The National Oceanographic Research Institute's West Sea Ocean Survey Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) announced that it would conduct surveys of the land topography around Gunsan Port and reflect the results in the latest charts.
The existing Gunsan Port chart left the Gunjang Industrial Complex area blank, causing inconvenience to users.
Accordingly, the West Sea Marine Survey Office conducted topographic surveys for the month of February on industrial infrastructure, roads, ports, and major buildings within the Gunjang National Industrial Complex (around Gunsan Port) using the principles of a navigation system that connects the Hydrographic Survey Data Processing System (Hypack) and the differential GPS (DGPS) receiver.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “By reflecting the Gunjang National Industrial Complex on the latest charts, it is expected that it will be used as very useful data for ships entering and leaving Gunsan Port and port-related personnel.”
The revised charts can be purchased from a chart sales agency (☎02-701-9981, 051-466-0760) or through the company's Internet website (www.chartkorea.com) starting in April.

ko-news-notices-347-8372c75064.title: Providing underwater information in the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay
ko-news-notices-347-8372c75064.text:
Providing underwater information in the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay
2022-03-02
National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it will distribute a product containing the latest submarine topography information on the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay.
The undersea topography information provided this time includes various marine information such as precise undersea topography, distribution of shallow strata, distribution of surface sediments, sediment grain-size distribution, tides, and tidal currents surveyed last year in the Deokjeokdo, Daeijakdo, and Seongapdo areas in the southern part of Gyeonggi Province using cutting-edge marine survey equipment such as multi-beam echo sounders.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “The results of seafloor information in coastal waters are used as data for chart correction, provision of navigational information, and selection of suitable sites for artificial reefs, and are expected to be provided as important information needed for review of coastal waters and planning new routes.”
Meanwhile, this outcome will be distributed to government agencies and marine research institutes, and will be used as basic data for coastal development and conservation, and construction of basic marine geographical information.

ko-news-notices-348-8372c75064.title: Southwest Coast development plans abound in rosy visions
ko-news-notices-348-8372c75064.text:
The southwest coast development plan only shows a rosy picture.
2022-03-02
The southwestern coastal region, from Incheon through Pyeongtaek and Saemangeum to Yeongam and Haenam, is awash with rosy development visions.
All kinds of development plans are being promoted based on the justification of the emergence of the Pan-Yellow Sea economic zone and balanced national development.
In particular, various development projects are complexly intertwined in the Honam and southwestern coastal regions.
What the government has put forward is the ‘Southwest Coast Comprehensive Development Plan’, also called the S Project.
A total of 22.4 trillion won will be invested over 14 years from this year to 2020 to develop the Muan, Mokpo, and Shinan regions into industrial bases in the Yellow Sea Rim region.
Within the S Project, the Saemangeum area is planned to be developed into an agricultural and industrial complex.
The government claims that if this development plan is implemented as scheduled and the area is developed into an industrial and logistics hub with a population of 600,000, it will become one of the central regions of the Yellow Sea Rim Economic Area.
Jeonnam Province is promoting the J Project separately from the government’s S Project.
Project J plans to build an F1 racetrack, marine leisure town, health recreation town, and golf course on 30 million pyeong of land in Samho-eup, Yeongam-gun and Sanmyeon, Haenam-gun by 2016.
The total investment amount is 35 trillion won, and it is a tourism and leisure complex city that will accommodate 300,000 people.
In addition, development plans such as Naju Innovation City and Jangseong Honam Logistics Base are also being promoted.
Commenting on these proliferating development plans, Kim Eui-jun, a professor at the Department of Community Development at Seoul National University, said, “In Muan Enterprise City, investment from domestic companies and foreign countries is currently unclear, and Muan Airport has also spent tens of billions of won to build facilities, but is not even able to open.” He added, “It is problematic to pour out development plans like this when the investment entity has not been confirmed.”
An official from the Ministry of Construction and Transportation said, "The justification for balanced regional development is good, but the problem is that this plan is being promoted individually without any master plan." He added, "A development plan that can efficiently connect nearby areas, including Saemangeum, must be developed."
[Planning Reporting Team = Deputy Editor Chae Gyeong-ok (team leader) / Kim Ki-cheol (real estate desk) / Kim Gyu-sik (business desk)]

ko-news-notices-349-8372c75064.title: After the Three Gorges Dam began full-scale impoundment...
ko-news-notices-349-8372c75064.text:
After the full-scale water blocking of the Three Gorges Dam...
2022-03-02
The Yellow Sea and East China Sea are showing signs of significant change due to the Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze River. This dam, the world's largest, entered full-scale impoundment in 2004 and is the lifeline that accounts for 80% of the fresh water flowing into the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
On the 22nd, the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries announced the results of the ‘Study on the Marine Environment Impact of the Construction of the Three Gorges Dam in the South Sea (East China Sea)’ conducted between 2003 and 2006 by the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute (KORDI) and the National Institute of Fisheries Science.
The most noticeable phenomenon after water blocking discovered in this study is the decrease in suspended solids. The suspended solids concentration, which was 3.261 mg/l in 2004, decreased by more than 20% to 1.791 mg/l the following year. The problem is that the nitrogen content in suspended solids is a nutrient that the Yellow Sea desperately needs. The report stated that the decrease in suspended solids, which are nutrients for phytoplankton, will have a significant impact on the marine ecosystem, including fish.
According to a Chinese study, the construction of the Three Gorges Dam is expected to reduce suspended sediments by 23.4%, equivalent to an annual average of 110 million tons, resulting in a 10% decrease in nutrients supplied to the sea.
In addition, the study predicted that the Three Gorges Dam would release more water in the spring, the dry season, and reduce outflow in the summer, the flood season, so that the summer salinity concentration would increase to about 1% at the mouth of the Yangtze River and about 0.04% on the west side of Jeju Island.
Observations showed that lumps of low-salinity water in the Yangtze River frequently approach the waters around Jeju Island. These low-salinity water masses are freshwater that has not yet mixed with seawater; they often trigger red tides and mass fish deaths in the South Sea and around Jeju Island.
Principal Researcher Choi Dong-rim of KORDI, who led the study, said, “Changes in water temperature and salinity concentration can only be identified through longer-term studies. In the second phase of the study, which started this year, we plan to conduct a quantitative analysis of the impact on ecosystems such as fishing grounds and changes in seawater characteristics.”
Hongseop Cho, environmental reporter ecothink@hani.co.kr

ko-news-notices-351-8372c75064.title: Distribution of BADA MAP trial version
ko-news-notices-351-8372c75064.text:
Distribution of BADA MAP trial version
2022-03-02
National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it plans to distribute a trial version of the BADA Map, developed to popularize electronic navigation charts, in the middle of this month.
The National Oceanographic Research Institute developed a sea map (BADA Map) program that can automatically convert electronic charts into various formats (DXF, SHP, SVC, TXT), allowing the general public to use electronic charts even in a typical PC environment.
Electronic charts have so far been used only for navigation, and the generalization of the GIS concept has increased the number of users. However, due to the unique nature of having to use dedicated hardware and software, it has been difficult for those who use them for academic or leisure purposes.
Accordingly, the National Oceanographic Research Institute developed a sea map and decided to distribute an evaluation version of the pilot program to a limited number of users to improve performance.
The evaluation version contains about 20 electronic charts of Korea's southeastern and southern coasts converted into various formats, and includes functions to easily extract water depth and coastline.
Applicants will be accepted for the evaluation version through the agency website (www.nori.go.kr) from the 5th to the 13th of this month, and 100 people will be selected according to the purpose of using electronic navigation charts and distributed from the middle of this month.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “To improve the performance of the ocean map, we plan to conduct a survey in June of selected pilot users, supplement the improvements, and distribute it to the entire public starting in October.”
For inquiries regarding ocean maps, please contact the National Oceanographic Research Institute electronic chart team (032-880-0551~2).

ko-news-notices-353-8372c75064.title: NORI and UNSW develop a tidal prediction model for the Yellow Sea
ko-news-notices-353-8372c75064.text:
NORI and UNSW develop a tidal prediction model for the Yellow Sea
2022-03-02
The National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced joint research with the University of New South Wales (UNSW) in Australia to develop a numerical model capable of forecasting tides in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
The collaboration was proposed by UNSW. Dr Do-seong Byun of the agency's research laboratory was dispatched to UNSW from February 15 to March 30 and worked with the team led by Professor Wang So-hwa (H. X. Wang), one of the world's leading scientists in sediment-transport modeling.
The two institutions first developed a numerical model that forecasts tides and tidal currents in the offshore Yellow Sea. Building on this work they plan to add functionality that accurately represents the repeated exposure and inundation of intertidal areas with the tides.
A successful model would improve prediction of tidal sea level changes in the Yellow Sea where shallow water and a large tidal range produce extensive intertidal flats.
Byun said that the team planned to improve the model using offshore Yellow Sea level observations that the agency would collect for the first time that year. He expected the model to enable offshore tide and tidal-current forecasts not previously available and to support high-accuracy bathymetric surveys.

ko-news-notices-354-8372c75064.title: Operation of a real-time navigation safety information collection system
ko-news-notices-354-8372c75064.text:
Operation of a real-time navigation safety information collection system
2022-03-02
National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has developed a real-time web-based navigation information collection system to quickly collect and provide navigation safety information and will begin operating it on the 9th.
The navigation information system has improved the navigational beacon facility information that had been collected from each regional maritime affairs and fisheries office in an off-line manner into a real-time collection system in a web environment, creating a quick and convenient navigation safety information system.
Information on navigational beacon facilities has been provided through the Notices to Mariners issued weekly by NORI for the safe navigation of ships. However, as information provided by each local office was processed in off-line documents, the information collection system was not automated, causing delays in information collection and the inconvenience of not being able to immediately utilize the collected information.
This developed collection system was built in conjunction with the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Business Management System (OKIS), and when new changes are entered, they are automatically converted into Notices to Mariners and DB managed in real time. In addition, by linking with the electronic approval system, official document work is minimized and all system users can jointly utilize the information.
A NORI official said, “Currently, we have completed the development of only the aids to navigation information, which accounts for about 70% of the total Notice to Mariners information. In the future, we plan to expand it to include information that affects all maritime traffic, such as port construction and shooting training, and convert Notices to Mariners information collection and services to a real-time system.”

ko-news-notices-356-8372c75064.title: Precision hydrographic survey of major ports on the west coast
ko-news-notices-356-8372c75064.text:
Precision hydrographic survey of major ports on the west coast
2022-03-02
The National Oceanographic Research Institute's West Sea Survey Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) announced that it will conduct precise hydrographic surveys at Gunsan, Janghang Port, Pyeongtaek Port, and Daeheuksando Port for five months from this month to August to ensure safe navigation of ships.
In this survey, we plan to conduct a detailed survey of the water depth, seabed sediment, rocks exposed at low tide, coastline, etc. for a 1,300km sea area using the latest hydrographic survey equipment such as precision echo sounder and differential GPS (DGPS) receiver for ports and access channels where ships frequently pass.
Gunsan Port, Janghang Port, and Pyeongtaek Port are sea areas that require periodic and precise water depth information as they are topographically ports with large variations in seafloor topography.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “We will quickly provide information to navigators through Notices to Mariners regarding rapid changes in water depth revealed in this survey, and provide basic data for maritime traffic safety for ships using West Coast ports and development of the maritime and fisheries industries through chart revision.”

ko-news-notices-357-8372c75064.title: Opening of Janghang Port marine research vessel and tide observatory in commemoration of Ocean Day
ko-news-notices-357-8372c75064.text:
Opening of Janghang Port marine research vessel and tide observatory in commemoration of Ocean Day
2022-03-02
The National Oceanographic Research Institute's West Sea Ocean Research Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) opens its oceanographic research vessel and tide station to celebrate Ocean Day.
The West Sea Ocean Research Office has decided to open the ocean research vessel Hwanghae Ro (77 tons) and the Janghang Port Tide Observatory at Janghang Port on the 31st in order to increase understanding of the ocean to students and the general public.
On this day, citizens will be able to see the latest navigation equipment such as automatic navigation devices and electronic chart systems installed on ships, as well as cutting-edge marine research equipment and facilities such as multibeam echo sounding equipment and undersea obstacle detectors that can three-dimensionally explore the undersea terrain and find obstacles, giving them a variety of experiences in the field of marine surveys.
In addition, at the Janghang Port Tide Observatory, you can realistically experience the principles of rising and falling sea water through a tour of tide observation equipment and an introduction to the real-time tide information service system.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “We have opened the research vessel to inform the general public about the importance of the sea and to provide an opportunity for young people to develop an enterprising maritime spirit.” He added, “Visitors will have a variety of experiences about ocean research.”
Individuals and groups wishing to participate in the event may apply to the West Sea Ocean Research Office (041-956-2010).

ko-news-notices-358-8372c75064.title: East Sea surface temperature rises by 0.06°C a year
ko-news-notices-358-8372c75064.text:
East Sea water temperature rises by 0.06 degrees every year
2022-03-02
Coastal sea levels have risen by 3.2 mm per year over the past 30 years.
It was found that the surface water temperature of the East Sea has increased by about 2℃ over the past 100 years. Additionally, it was found that over the past 30 years, the sea level along Korea's coast has risen by 3.2 mm per year.
Lee Jae-hak, head of the Marine Climate Change Research Group at the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute (KORDI), announced the results of the ‘Study on the Mid- to Long-Term Fluctuation Response of the East Sea Due to Climate Change’ focusing on these details at the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries on the 28th.
According to research results, since the surface water temperature of the East Sea increased in the 1940s, there has been a large increase of 0.06℃ every year since the mid-1980s.
Unlike in the 1940s, when water temperature rise was limited to winter, water temperature is now rising regardless of the season, and this phenomenon is especially noticeable in the northwestern waters of the East Sea.
The study also found that rising water temperatures were raising sea level not only along the East Sea coast but also in its interior, primarily through thermal expansion.
In addition, it was found that sea levels along the coasts of Korea and Japan have risen by 3.2 mm per year over the past 30 years.
In particular, it has risen 6.5mm per year over the past 9 years and 6.4mm over the past 14 years, showing a high rate of increase since the 1990s, and this has been maintained until recently.
This rise in water temperature and sea level is higher than the average value of global ocean change (water temperature about 0.04℃/year, sea level 3.1mm/year), meaning that the seas around Korea are responding greatly to climate change.
According to recent research results at home and abroad, the East Sea has a clear tendency for long-term fluctuations to the extent that changes can be detected at depth as well as at the surface, and recent changes in the marine ecosystem support this cause.
Director Lee said, “It is necessary to prepare mid- to long-term national policies to prevent disasters such as coastal flooding, coastal erosion, and port flooding due to marine climate change, and to respond to changes in the marine ecosystem and fish farm environment,” and added, “In particular, it is urgent to prepare a response to marine change by presenting a national standard marine change scenario.”

ko-news-notices-359-8372c75064.title: New chart issued for Korea's southern coast and nearby waters
ko-news-notices-359-8372c75064.text:
Publication of new charts in and around the South Sea of ​​Korea
2022-03-02
Reflects the latest water depth information from Busan Port to Mokpo Port and Jeju Island
The National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has published a new chart reflecting the latest water depth information for waters along the route from Busan Port to Mokpo Port and around Jeju Island to ensure safe navigation of ships.
The new chart (scale 1/500,000) lists territorial sea limits, straight baselines, specific sea areas, and fisheries resource protection zones. It is expected to greatly contribute to safe navigation as it contains various up-to-date information such as seabed depth necessary for safe navigation of vessels engaged in fishing activities in coastal waters of Korea.
The newly published chart (chart number S-No. 418) was published based on the results of a survey of the seabed topography of the sea area around Jeju Island, covering 31,000 ㎢, using the 700-ton marine research vessel “Badaro No. 1” equipped with cutting-edge hydrographic survey equipment such as shallow sea exploration equipment (EM3000) and deep sea exploration equipment (EM300).
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “We plan to quickly produce and distribute the latest charts for Korea’s coastal waters to ensure maritime traffic safety.”
Charts can be purchased through a chart sales agency (☎02-701-9981, 051-466-0760) or through the company's Internet website (www.chartkorea.com).

ko-news-notices-360-8372c75064.title: Geographical information of the sea and land at a glance
ko-news-notices-360-8372c75064.text:
Geographical information of the sea and land at a glance
2022-03-02
Started production of port basic map
National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has begun production of port maps for Mokpo and Donghae Ports, which contain various geographical information of the sea and land.
The port basic map is a drawing that contains information such as land topography and features shown on the map, detailed water depth of the seabed shown on the chart, various port geographical information, coastline, maritime boundaries, tides, currents, etc. in a systematic and scientific manner, making it possible to view various geographical information at a glance.
In order to build a marine geographic information base for Korea's jurisdictional waters, National Oceanographic Research Institute has produced and distributed port basic maps for 17 trade ports, including Incheon Port, Busan, Gwangyang, and Ulsan, starting in 2001.
We plan to complete the production of basic maps for Korea's 28 trade ports, 51 coastal ports, and coastal waters by 2010.
An official from the National Oceanographic Research Institute said, “The port basic map is expected to be used as important data to support marine and fisheries policies such as port operation, marine development, and marine environment conservation,” and added, “By linking it with the currently underway National Geographic Information System (NGIS) construction project, it will contribute to the implementation of e-government by completing a digital national land where the sea and land become one.”

ko-news-notices-361-8372c75064.title: Development of a marine survey information system based on marine GIS
ko-news-notices-361-8372c75064.text:
Development of a marine survey information system based on marine GIS
2022-03-02
Providing convenient and rapid marine geographical information services by building digital marine information
The National Oceanographic Research Institute (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that starting this month, it has begun developing a marine geographic information system (GIS) that links the vast amount of data obtained through marine surveys with digital maps to create a database.
Marine GIS is a system that conveniently and quickly provides various marine geographical information by linking various information related to the sea with location information, creating a spatial database, and constructing GIS. It is used for marine policy, marine development and use, navigation safety, and national defense affairs.
The National Oceanographic Research Institute has been working on establishing marine GIS from 2001 to 2006, and this project is a second-stage improvement project to be carried out until 2010, and plans to invest 1.1 billion won this year to build an integrated database of vast marine survey information.
In addition, we plan to convert marine place names into a database and build a database for paper charts and original charts that have not been digitized.
In particular, a basic marine GIS for the seabed topography of the East Sea region will be established, detailed information on the seabed topography of the sea, coast, and port will be accumulated, and a national marine basic GIS management program containing information such as seabed topography and coastline will also be developed.
Meanwhile, the National Oceanographic Research Institute is running an open contest for a brand for the ocean research information system through the National Oceanographic Research Institute's website (www.nori.go.kr) until the 22nd of this month.
It must be a unique and easily memorable brand while pursuing the image of a world-class digital advanced marine research information, and we plan to select one person each for Best, Excellence, and 10 lucky winners on the 30th of this month to award awards.

ko-news-notices-362-8372c75064.title: Busan North Port redevelopment plan narrowed to two alternatives
ko-news-notices-362-8372c75064.text:
Two plans for Busan North Port redevelopment master plan compressed
2022-03-02
The Busan North Port redevelopment master plan has been prepared as ‘Plan 1’, which focuses on securing waterfront space and views, and ‘Plan 2’, which focuses on expanding commercial functions, and will be subject to public opinion survey by Busan citizens.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Busan Port Authority (BPA) held a 'Busan North Port Master Plan Amendment Briefing Session' on the afternoon of the 11th and announced the redevelopment direction focusing on these contents. Prior to this, the government reaffirmed the principle of “promoting an eco-friendly plan that maximizes the use of existing docks and minimizes sea reclamation.”
The revised master plan released on this day decided to exclude the international exchange, commercial, and business districts, including high-rise buildings, proposed in the existing master plan from the first stage (Piers 1 to 4, Central Pier) redevelopment plan starting next year, and instead include them in the second stage Jaseongdae Pier redevelopment plan to begin in 2020.
Plan 1 focuses on expanding waterfront space, and plan 2 focuses on expanding commercial functions.
First, ‘Plan 1’ is a medium-low density development plan that minimizes land reclamation by creating a deck-type waterfront space on the central pier connected to Busan Station and creating an island-style landmark in the form of an artificial island. In particular, of the 1.42 million ㎡ of the redevelopment district, public land including waterfront spaces is 1.03 million ㎡ (73%), which is 12% more than the existing plan's 870,000 ㎡ (61%), while the reclaimed area is 557,000 ㎡, smaller than the existing plan (624,000 ㎡) to enable environmentally friendly development.
‘Plan 2’ is a plan that takes commercial functions into consideration, and plans to place a ‘mixed-use port district’ ​​that integrates the Nampo-dong commercial district, commercial business district, and port functions on Pier 2, and use Pier 2 as a cruise terminal. It was decided to leave the front of Piers 3 and 4 as a development reserve so that it can be developed into a maritime cultural district in the future.
The total project cost was estimated to be 7.99 trillion won (KRW 1.51 trillion in infrastructure costs) for plan 1, and 8.17 trillion won (KRW 1.53 trillion in infrastructure costs) for plan 2.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and BPA plan to provide sufficient data and information on these two plans to those surveyed within this month, then collect public opinion through a public opinion survey, finalize the redevelopment plan, and begin the project within next year after announcing the basic plan and drafting a business plan in September.
Lee Jae-gyun, head of the Port Redevelopment Promotion Planning Group of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, said on this day, “The existing master plan announced at the end of last year had problems such as blocking sea views and access opportunities, but this plan has been prepared as an environmentally friendly plan by improving these problems.” He added, “We plan to collect a wide range of citizen opinions to ensure that the North Port redevelopment project is promoted without a hitch.”

ko-news-notices-363-8372c75064.title: Greenhouse gases: Korea nears mandatory reduction targets, too
ko-news-notices-363-8372c75064.text:
Greenhouse gases: Korea nears mandatory reduction targets, too
2022-03-02
Greenhouse gases: Korea nears mandatory reduction targets, too
[[CO2 is money] Certain to be included in the second reduction target starting in 2013]
More than 100 people have died in India and Pakistan due to extreme heat of up to 52 degrees Celsius. In the southeastern region, including Florida, the lake has run out due to a drought not seen in 112 years. In southeastern China, 66 people died due to record-breaking rain. Australia was hit by a storm not seen in 30 years, killing about 10 people.
These are the world-wide abnormal weather events reported in June. Such incidents are increasing every year. The biggest cause of extreme weather is global warming. Scientists warn that if greenhouse gases, the main cause of warming, are not reduced, abnormal weather events will further increase.
Preparations for global warming have already begun worldwide. Through the 1992 Climate Change Convention and the 2005 Kyoto Protocol, developed countries are obliged to reduce greenhouse gases. Developing countries, including Korea, are also making efforts to reduce greenhouse gases. The Earth is currently at war with greenhouse gases.
On April 6th, people around the world heard a shocking report. This was the future image of the Earth predicted by the United Nations' Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
"If the temperature rises by 1 degree Celsius in the 2020s, 400 million to 1.7 billion people worldwide will experience water shortages. Changes will occur in the composition of biological species, including the extinction of amphibians. Tropical infectious diseases such as malaria and allergies will become rampant around the world.
By 2080, global temperatures will rise by more than 3 degrees, causing 1.1 to 3.2 billion people to suffer from water shortages. 20% of the world's population is affected by floods. Most of Earth's creatures are at risk of extinction. “The sea level will rise by 24cm compared to now, and more than 30% of the coastal area will be lost.”
The premise of this report is ‘if warming continues at the current rate.’ The IPCC stated that greenhouse gas emissions should begin to decline after peaking in 2015. This means that there is not much time left to save the Earth.
After this report, interest in warming is increasing again.
◆Kyoto Protocol, obliging 38 countries to reduce greenhouse gases= With the Climate Change Agreement signed in 1992, developed countries decided to voluntarily reduce greenhouse gases.
However, the need to enforce more practical efforts was raised. This is the background to the birth of the Kyoto Protocol. The Kyoto Protocol, which came into effect in February 2005, stipulates who will reduce greenhouse gases, by how much, and how. According to the Kyoto Protocol, 38 countries are required to reduce emissions by an average of 5.2% compared to 1990 emissions from 2008 to 2012, although there are differences depending on each country's economic conditions.
Recently, discussions on reducing greenhouse gases have become more active because mandatory reductions will begin next year.
The Kyoto Protocol recognized the limitations of developed countries in carrying out all of their reduction obligations domestically, and introduced the Joint Implementation System (JI), Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), and Emissions Trading System (ET) to reduce greenhouse gases effectively and economically. This is the so-called Kyoto mechanism.
The joint implementation system is a system that recognizes the joint performance of greenhouse gas reduction projects among countries with mandatory reductions. This is a method of recognizing a portion of the greenhouse gas reductions reduced by one country by investing in another country as the reduction performance of the investing country.
The Clean Development Mechanism allows countries with mandatory reductions to use a portion of the results achieved through greenhouse gas reduction projects in developing countries as reductions in developed countries. Developed countries can use this to reduce greenhouse gases, and developing countries can receive technology and financial support from developed countries. In particular, unlike the joint implementation system, it recognizes early reduction activities before the first mandatory period, so it is already being actively carried out around the world.
The emissions trading system is a system that allows greenhouse gas reductions to be traded like market products. If the reduction exceeds the mandatory reduction amount, it can be sold, and if it is not achieved, the shortfall can be met by purchasing it. It is designed to minimize overall reduction costs by reducing emissions as much as possible and making profits from selling emissions permits, or choosing to purchase emissions permits if it is cheaper than reducing emissions.
◆Post-Kyoto Protocol discussion... Korea also faces imminent mandatory reduction = The first reduction period of the Kyoto Protocol ends in 2012. Accordingly, discussions on the post-Kyoto system after 2012 began at the 12th General Assembly of the Parties to the Framework Convention on Climate Change held in Nairobi, Kenya in November 2006.
In particular, as the recent G8 summit decided to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 50% compared to 1990 by 2050, discussions on the ‘post-Kyoto Protocol’ are expected to begin in earnest. In addition, the recent change in position of the United States, which had refused to ratify the Kyoto Protocol, is expected to act as a catalyst. The United States has proposed holding a meeting of 15 large emitting countries, including India and China, in addition to the G8, to set long-term goals by the end of 2008.
There is a high possibility that Korea, which was not a country with mandatory reductions under the Kyoto Protocol, will be included as a country with mandatory reductions in the post-Kyoto Protocol discussions. This is why we need to pay attention to the post-Kyoto Protocol.
Korea ranks 9th in the world in greenhouse gas emissions (as of 2002), and among OECD countries, the only countries not subject to mandatory reduction are Korea and Mexico, so we have been under pressure to be included in the mandatory reduction countries. Moreover, as Mexico is known to be planning to introduce a voluntary reduction plan soon, experts have a common view that Korea will soon become a country with mandatory reductions.
In particular, public opinion is spreading that voluntary efforts to reduce greenhouse gases are necessary, regardless of whether countries are included in mandatory reductions. The Korea Environmental Policy Evaluation Institute analyzed that if no measures to reduce greenhouse gases are implemented, the Korean Peninsula will suffer economic damage worth 58 trillion won per year due to temperature rises in 2100.
Accordingly, our government is also preparing a realistically achievable obligation to minimize the social and economic costs that will arise from the obligation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

ko-news-notices-364-8372c75064.title: Desalination plants can worsen water shortages
ko-news-notices-364-8372c75064.text:
‘Desalination plants can worsen water shortages’
2022-03-02
Environment] ‘Desalination plants can worsen water shortages’ [WWF] [Yonhap] The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) warned on the 19th that the method of removing salt from seawater and converting it into drinking water will further contribute to water shortage.
WWF claims that the method of obtaining water by evaporating seawater not only uses a lot of energy, but also emits a lot of greenhouse gases, which ultimately further reduces the supply of fresh water.
The organization emphasized that countries with water shortages, such as Spain, Saudi Arabia, and Australia, should use water conservation and recycling methods and avoid large desalination facilities, which have been pointed out as a cause of environmental pollution and destruction of the ecosystem. WWF's warning coincided with Australia's announcement of plans to build the world's largest desalination plant.
WWF pointed out, "The appeal of being able to obtain water anywhere through desalination is based on a misunderstanding, which is likely to divert the public's attention, policies, and budgets in the wrong direction rather than wise water use."
Due to global warming, icebergs and glaciers, which account for 69% of the world's freshwater supply, are melting rapidly and droughts are expected to worsen, so it is expected that more and more investment will be made in desalination technology.
WWF pointed out that some farmers are using desalinated water to grow water-intensive crops in naturally dry regions, pointing out that this is an inappropriate trend considering high energy costs, and criticized, "Farming with desalinated water is not economically feasible in any region." Many areas still have cheaper and better ways to replenish water that are less harmful to the environment.
WWF currently estimates the number of desalination facilities around the world to be more than 10,000 and predicts that the number will increase exponentially in the next few years as countries with rapidly expanding arid regions, such as the United States, India, and China, seek ways to supply water.
Currently, about half of the desalination facilities are located in the Gulf region, where rich oil-producing countries meet 60% of their water needs with desalinated water.
Australian cities also rely heavily on desalination facilities, and Spain also uses desalinated water extensively for real estate development, agricultural purposes, and even for golf courses along the Mediterranean coast.
WWF said that large-scale desalination facilities are threatening marine life and called for further research into how the high-salinity brine discharged after desalination affects marine life and ecosystems.
WWF emphasized that although desalination facilities may be important in some cases, such as environments with a lot of mixed water, the construction of large-scale desalination facilities must be approved after thorough feasibility and environmental verification.
(Geneva Reuters = Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-365-8372c75064.title: Saemangeum to be developed as an eco-friendly mixed-use city
ko-news-notices-365-8372c75064.text:
“Saemangeum to be developed as an eco-friendly mixed-use city”
2022-03-02
“Saemangeum, developed into an environmentally friendly complex city” (comprehensive)
Jeonbuk-do confirms Saemangeum special bill
(Jeonju = Yonhap News) Reporter Baek Do-in = On the 5th, Jeonbuk-do finalized and announced the 'Saemangeum Comprehensive Development Special Bill (hereinafter referred to as Saemangeum Special Bill)', which aims to develop the Saemangeum area into an environmentally friendly mixed-use city and designate part of it as a free economic zone.
The Saemangeum Special Bill was prepared through a coordination process with the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, related ministries and political circles based on a draft commissioned by the Jeonbuk Development Institute, a research institute under the provincial government, and consists of a total of 9 chapters and 46 articles.
The Saemangeum Special Act consists of ▲Chapter 1 General Provisions ▲Chapter 2 Establishment of Saemangeum Comprehensive Development Plan ▲Chapter 3 Designation of Saemangeum Comprehensive Development District ▲Chapter 4 Implementation of Saemangeum Comprehensive Development Project ▲Chapter 5 Special Provisions for Environment-Friendly Development ▲Chapter 6 Supplementary Provisions for Support for Development Projects ▲Chapter 7 Special Provisions for Designation of Free Economic Zones ▲Chapter 8 Supplementary Provisions ▲Chapter 9 is structured with penalties, etc.
The province states that the purpose of enacting the special law is to develop the Saemangeum area into an environmentally friendly complex city centered on housing, agriculture, tourism, industry and logistics, and to designate some of them as free economic zones to contribute to balanced national development and strengthening national competitiveness.
In Chapter 2, the province designated the Governor of Jeonbuk Province as the person with the authority to draft the development plan, which had differing opinions with the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, and summarized the project scope and target area of ​​the comprehensive development plan.
Chapter 3 contains the designation procedures for areas scheduled for development, conditions for de-designation, restrictions on various activities, etc., and Chapter 4 contains information that permitting and licensing procedures will be greatly simplified for rapid project implementation.
Chapter 5 contains regulations to designate environmental conservation management areas for environmentally friendly development, take special measures in areas where water pollution sources occur, and prepare measures to support resettled residents.
Chapter 6 includes proposals for the establishment and operation of special accounts to support development costs, tax and levy reductions, and granting of subsidies, and Chapter 7 includes designation and operation of free economic zones, support for investment attraction companies, and special provisions for land acquisition by foreigners.
The province explained that after unveiling the draft of the 'Saemangeum Comprehensive Development and International Investment Free Zone Special Act', which consists of a total of 7 chapters and 83 articles, at the end of last year, it decided on the final draft after consulting with the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, the Ministry of Finance and Economy, and the political circles for about two months.
The province has selected Rep. Kim Won-ki of the Uri Party as the lead sponsor of the bill and plans to secure additional sponsors by the 14th and then submit the bill to the National Assembly on the 15th.
However, relevant ministries such as the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and the Ministry of Finance and Economy are showing difficulty in enacting the law, and it is not easy to receive cooperation from the political circles ahead of the presidential election, so it is expected that there will be a difficult road before the actual bill is passed.
Deputy Governor for Administration Jeon Hee-jae said, "Reflecting the wishes of the people of Jeollabuk-do, we have focused on quickly developing the Saemangeum District into an economic center in the 21st century Yellow Sea Rim Economic Zone," and added, "We will concentrate all our capabilities to ensure that the bill is passed as soon as possible."

ko-news-notices-366-8372c75064.title: Installation of ‘floating breakwater’ off the coast of Tongyeong
ko-news-notices-366-8372c75064.text:
Installation of ‘floating breakwater’ off the coast of Tongyeong
2022-03-02
A floating wave-dissipating breakwater that reduces wave energy was installed in the sea off Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnam-do.
According to Tongyeong City on the 5th, a 200 m floating wave-dissipating breakwater, a type of breakwater that floats on the water and reduces waves, was installed and operated between Sojangdu Island and Yudo Island in Yeonhwa-ri, Sanyang-eup, which are crowded with offshore fishing grounds, last month.
8 billion won, including national and local funds, was invested in the construction of the floating breakwater, which began installation work in 2005.
This facility, made of steel, is hollow and can float on water. Each unit is 50 m long, 15 m wide, and 4 m high, and has four units connected to each other.
Out of the 4m height, 2.5m is designed to be submerged below the water, and is connected to an anchor installed under the sea, allowing it to move flexibly depending on wave conditions and direction.
Conventional breakwaters are built on stone foundations on the seabed, which takes more time and money and blocks seawater flow. The floating wave-dissipating structure is relatively inexpensive and allows seawater to circulate freely.
[Yonhap News]

ko-news-notices-367-8372c75064.title: Korea should bring climate change into public debate
ko-news-notices-367-8372c75064.text:
Korea should bring climate change into public debate
2022-03-02
Heads of diplomatic missions to the EU and Canada emphasized with one voice at a roundtable meeting
(Seoul = Yonhap News) Reporter Seo Dong-hee = "In discussions on reducing greenhouse gases, there will be limits to avoiding reduction obligations as before. As our national power has grown, the time has come to shoulder the corresponding international 'moral responsibility.'"
Ambassador Cho Chang-beom of Australia, Ambassador Jung Woo-sung of the Permanent Mission to the European Union (EU), and Shin Gil-soo, Consul General in Montreal and Ambassador of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), emphasized with one voice the necessity and urgency of bringing greenhouse gas reduction into public debate, considering the rapidly changing international community to address climate change.
Those who temporarily returned to Korea in 2007 to attend a meeting of heads of diplomatic missions abroad recently held a roundtable discussion at the downtown Plaza Hotel and emphasized, "We need to pursue environmentally friendly strategies on a consistent basis domestically to strengthen our 'environmental diplomacy' capabilities."
At the roundtable discussion moderated by Lee Byeong-wook, head of the LG Environmental Research Institute, the ambassadors vividly conveyed ▲ each country's perception of the seriousness of global warming ▲ trends of discussion within the international community based on this ▲ each country's government's perception of Korea's position, as they felt it in their host country.
Prior to the start of the discussion, Director Lee pointed out the background for the selection of Australia, the EU, and Canada, saying, "The EU is a leader, Canada is a party to the climate change convention but has recently changed its position, and Australia is a party to the convention but has not ratified the Kyoto Protocol."
Awareness of each country surrounding the seriousness of global warming was quite high.
Ambassador Cho of Australia said, "Australia has the highest incidence of skin cancer due to direct exposure to ozone due to geographical conditions, and over the past five years, droughts have occurred one after another, drying out river beds and causing large forest fires one after another."
Ambassador Cho continued, "Regarding the Murray-Darling River, which runs through the Australian continent, we are taking strong measures to save water resources, such as unifying the management of each state to the federal government and allocating 10 billion dollars (Australian) as a budget. The public is watching with great interest, and it will emerge as a major domestic political issue in the general election in October."
Ambassador Jung of the EU Delegation introduced that the EU is "leading the world's public opinion on the issue of climate change from the perspective of 'humanity's immediate environmental issue,'" and added, "The EU has a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 8% from 1990 levels in accordance with the Kyoto Protocol, and recently declared that it would reduce emissions by 20% from 1990 levels by 2020."
Ambassador Jung said the EU had gone a step further and was willing to reduce emissions by up to 30% if other countries participated. The ambassador added, "In fact, the EU has designated 11,500 sites that emit large amounts of greenhouse gases, such as power plants, and has begun taking action."
Regarding Canada, a signatory country to the Kyoto Protocol, which imposes greenhouse gas reduction obligations on developed countries, Consul General Shin explained, "Since the Conservative government took office last year, there has been interest in the Asia-Pacific Partnership (APP), which emphasizes long-term, voluntary reductions instead of the mandatory burden under the Kyoto Protocol. This is because the tar sands (oil sand) industry in Canada has recently become economically viable and is rapidly developing."
Consul General Shin continued, "Canada has been seriously affected by global warming due to the geographical condition that part of its territory is located in the Arctic Circle, so there has been a lot of interest across the country from the beginning," adding, "Civil society has a high interest and is always putting pressure on the government to actively respond to the problem."
How is the industry in that country reacting?
Ambassador Cho said, "Australia agrees with the general principle of 'joint response by the international community' to climate change, but is considering how to find a balance between the other goal of maintaining the competitiveness of the domestic industry. In Australia, which exports abundant natural resources, there is considerable pressure from the industry, so we are taking the position that we are not yet at the stage of taking legal obligations to protect the domestic industry."
Ambassador Cho also added, “The Australian government and academia argue that it is important to make practical efforts, such as developing science and technology, to curb greenhouse gas emissions, and that this is the right way to respond to climate change.”
Ambassador Jung said, “It is true that some industries and industrial policy departments are dissatisfied with the inclusion of ‘vehicle carbon dioxide emission suppression measures’ or ‘aviation sector emissions trading system’ according to the national greenhouse gas quota system.”
Ambassador Jeong, however, said, "Because environmental issues are an immediate problem for humanity, it appears that radical policies can be proposed and adopted, and more power is placed on the side that 'we must deal with it' rather than the industry's position."
He pointed out, “the EU believes that Korea should participate and is pressing it to do so,” adding, “Recently, the EU has created a third category called ‘developing countries that have developed to the level of developed countries’ rather than developed countries or developing countries, and is using it widely in official documents.”
Ambassador Jeong also said, "With the recent change in public opinion in the United States, such as the Democratic Party's victory in the midterm elections, if the United States also pledges to reduce greenhouse gases after 2012, the EU could be expected to align with the United States and press developing countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions."
Experts point out that, in relation to trends in discussions in the international community, a situation may arise where Korea is obligated not only to reduce greenhouse gases but also to transfer clean development technologies to developing countries.
Regarding the government's strategy in this regard, Consul General Shin said, "The government considers the climate change agreement system and APP as the two major axes in the field of environmental diplomacy, and its position is to participate equally in both axes."
Ambassador Cho emphasized, "I believe that the APP does not replace the Kyoto system, but rather has a complementary function. We also need to refer to the case of Australia, which is actively developing and investing in new technologies to voluntarily reduce greenhouse gases."
Ambassador Cho pointed out that "Korea is already 11th in the world in terms of greenhouse gas emissions," and said, "In order to actively take on international 'moral responsibilities' commensurate with national power, we must seek a third way and act as a bridge between developed and developing countries to actively respond to global 'important challenges of the 21st century.'"
Consul General Shin said, "In light of the fact that non-participation in the Kyoto Protocol is analyzed as a representative example of damaging trust in U.S. leadership, Korea should give the image of contributing positively to international and global environmental protection efforts rather than avoiding this issue."
Director Lee Byeong-wook emphasized, "Korea has not been legally obliged to reduce greenhouse gases due to its status as a developing country, but there is a possibility that it will soon be obliged to not only reduce greenhouse gases but also transfer clean development technology to developing countries, so it is urgent to establish measures."
He went on to say, "A new system to replace the Kyoto Protocol will be formed in 2012," and added, "With the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) proposing to Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon to hold a 'climate change summit,' discussions surrounding this issue will become a big issue in the international community this year."

ko-news-notices-368-8372c75064.title: ‘Bongi Kim Seon-dal’ selling East Sea seawater?
ko-news-notices-368-8372c75064.text:
‘Bongi Kim Seon-dal’ selling East Sea seawater?
2022-03-02
Development of deep sea water rich in minerals and other substances attracts attention as a future industry Japanese market worth 2 trillion won... About 10 domestic companies will participate, “We will achieve a market worth 1 trillion won”
The price of bottled water on the market (0.5 liter, 700-800 won) is already equivalent to the price of gasoline. As water resources emerge as an important factor influencing global economic development, deep ocean water is attracting attention as a future industry. Deep ocean water is water that exists in the deep sea of ​​more than 200 meters where sunlight cannot reach. Contains a lot of minerals.
The ‘Deep Marine Water Development and Management Act’, which had been dormant in the National Assembly for over two years since it was announced as legislation in 2004, was passed by the National Assembly’s Agriculture, Forestry, Oceans and Fisheries Committee on the 25th. If it is finally passed at the plenary session in August-September, product development related to deep ocean water is expected to begin in earnest. In Japan, the size of the deep ocean water industry exceeds 2 trillion won per year.
◆The east coast is specially suited for deep ocean water development.
Deep ocean water development is only possible on the east coast. Among the three seas, it is the only sea area with a depth of more than 200m. In fact, placards announcing the development of deep ocean water are posted all over the coasts of Goseong, Sokcho, Yangyang, and Gangneung in Gangwon-do and Yeongdeok and Uljin in Gyeongsangbuk-do. There are about 10 related companies. An official said, “As we are developing water as a public good, local governments or local public enterprises are leading the deep ocean water development project,” and added, “It is being carried out in a way that they are working together with private companies on product development.”
Watervis, invested by the Military Mutual Aid Association, said, “We will complete the plant facilities in Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do in the middle of next month.
“Starting in the second half of the year, we will launch cosmetics made with deep ocean water drawn from a depth of 1,100 meters at a site about 18 km offshore from Yangyang,” the company announced on the 27th. Watervis, along with Lotte Chilsung Beverage, will also introduce a deep ocean water mixed drink.
Ulleung Mineral, which received venture investment from 48 people, plans to raise water from a depth of 650m in the sea near Ulleungdo Island, remove salts, and develop and sell bottled water, functional drinks, and cosmetics. This company has been selling functional salt extracted from deep water at department stores since last year. Gangwon Deep Water, a joint venture between Gangwon Goseong-gun and Daekyo, will soon build a plant and prepare to launch commercial products.
◆Japanese market size is around 2 trillion won
Globally, deep ocean water development is active in the United States (Hawaii) and Japan (Okinawa). In Japan, related products are being produced not only in bottled water but also in cosmetics, shochu, tofu, salt, and foods. Yong-sik Chu, CEO of Watervis, said, “We will create a market worth more than 1 trillion won in 2010,” and added, “I believe that the domestic market will also see the development of various products in food, medicine, agriculture, beauty, fisheries, etc. starting this year.”
◆The price must be lowered to become popular.
Among companies, in addition to Lotte Chilsung Beverage, Kooksoondang, Aekyung, Hyundai Pharmaceuticals, and Jinro are also exploring the possibility of commercialization with deep sea water developers.
But the high price is an obstacle. An official from the liquor industry pointed out, “Although research results from Japan have shown that deep water is good for the body, product prices may rise due to high logistics costs and deep ocean water development costs.” Kim Hong-gi, CEO of Ulleung Mineral, said, “We expect the price to be around 1,500 won for 500 ml of drinking water,” and added, “It is much lower than the price of products related to deep sea water imported into Korea.” Kim Hyeon-joo, director of Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute (KORDI)'s Deep Ocean Water Research Division, said, "If it becomes as popular as Japan, the prices of deep water-related products will be set at a level that is 10 to 20 percent higher than existing products."
Keyword… Deep ocean water = Contains large amounts of over 70 types of magnesium, calcium, and potassium that are necessary for the human body. To be economically viable, a deep sea must be located close to land, such as the East Sea. In addition to Korea, deep water development is active in the United States, Japan, Norway, and Taiwan. Japan has been developing deep water since the 1970s, and research results show that it has been effective in health, beauty, and atopic dermatitis treatment.
2007-06-28 Chosun Ilbo [Reporter Ho Gyeong-eop hok@chosun.com]

ko-news-notices-369-8372c75064.title: Reflection of convenience for the elderly and infirm in beach evaluations
ko-news-notices-369-8372c75064.text:
Reflection of convenience for the elderly and infirm in beach evaluations
2022-03-02
Starting from the 1st of next month, major beaches across the country will open sequentially. Major beaches in Busan, Jeju, and the south coast open in early July, and major beaches on the east coast open in mid-July, and during the opening period, various festivals tailored to the characteristics of each region are held.
Starting this year, use and accessibility, such as the installation of convenience facilities for underprivileged groups such as the elderly and the disabled, will be reflected in beach evaluations, and the ‘Citizen Participation Management System (BAP)’, which involves private participation in beach management and operation, will be expanded to 16 beaches nationwide.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries announced the ‘2007 National Beach Evaluation Plan’ on the 28th to encourage improvement of facilities, environment, and services through friendly competition at each beach prior to the opening of the beach.
The evaluation will be conducted on 45 beaches nationwide, among 351 beaches nationwide, applied by local governments, in four areas: ▲ operation and management ▲ environment, water quality and scenery ▲ safety management ▲ facilities.
According to the plan, starting this year, in order to help underprivileged groups such as the elderly and the disabled use the beach, the installation and operation of convenience facilities for the elderly and the operation of information services and helper systems will be newly reflected in the evaluation.
In addition, it was decided to introduce a beach evaluation monitoring system to increase transparency in beach evaluation and complement the limitations of one-time visits and written evaluations.
To this end, we plan to recruit about 30 beach evaluation monitors for each beach through the Internet, provide some of the summer vacation expenses to them, and submit the results of activities such as unfair fees and inconveniences to use for beach evaluation and system improvement.
In addition, as the beach ‘Citizen Participation Management System (BAP: Beach Adopt Program)’, which was piloted at Haeundae and Muchangpo Beach last year to encourage private participation in the management and operation of beaches, was evaluated to be effective, it was decided to expand the implementation to 16 beaches nationwide this year.
Places where the citizen participation management system is being introduced include Haeundae/Songjeong Beach (GS Construction), Mangsang Beach (Shinhan Card), Sokcho Beach (BC Card, E-Mart), Sampo Beach (Dongkwang Development), Jigyeong Beach (Daegyo Noonnoppi), Chunjangdae Beach (Seocheon Thermal Power Plant), Muchangpo Beach (Tourism Council, Marine Rescue Group), Daecheon Beach (Daecheon Tourism Association), Mallipo Beach (Cheonripo Arboretum), Mongsanpo Beach (Nammyeon Fisheries Cooperative), Yeonpo Beach (Geunhong Nonghyup), Iho Beach (Iho Land), Hamdeok Beach (Hamdeok Fishing Village), Pyoseon Beach (Pyoseon Fishing Village), Jungmun Beach (Lotte Hotel), There are 16 beaches nationwide, including Yulpo Beach (Hoecheon Youth Association).
In particular, in this evaluation, the majority of citizens often decide their preferences based on unfair charges and unfriendliness rather than facilities and environment, so we plan to increase local residents' willingness to self-manage through a weighty evaluation of this area.
As a result of the evaluation, we plan to provide various incentives, including support for facility improvement project costs of 600 million won, for excellent beaches.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries plans to enact the ‘Beach Management Act’ next year to establish institutional arrangements for the management, operation and safety of beaches.
Recruitment of beach evaluation monitors and beach-related information are provided in detail on the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries website (www.momaf.go.kr) and Sea Tour (www.seantour.com).

ko-news-notices-370-8372c75064.title: KRW 5 billion provided for development of new marine and fisheries technologies
ko-news-notices-370-8372c75064.text:
KRW 5 billion provided for development of new marine and fisheries technologies
2022-03-02
This year, the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries will provide a total of 5 billion won to new technology development projects in the marine and fisheries field, including 3.04 billion won (9 projects) for fisheries-specific research and development projects and 2 billion won (26 projects) to technology development projects for marine and fisheries small and medium-sized venture companies.
Among these, the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Small and Medium Business Administration raised KRW 2 billion, with the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Small and Medium Business Administration each raising KRW 1 billion, for the first time in the government for the technology development support project for maritime and fishery small and medium-sized venture companies, which is evaluated as presenting a new model as an inter-ministerial cooperation project.
87 companies applied for this project and 26 companies were selected, and the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Small and Medium Business Administration will manage 13 each.
The government will support 75% of research and development costs, and the research period will be one year. If the project is successfully completed, 20% of the government contribution will be paid as a technology fee.
In addition, in order to promote mechanization of fishing sites and develop fisheries technology, the main research institute was selected for nine designated fisheries-specific research and technology development projects.
This project will provide a total of 3.04 billion won over 1 to 3 years, and 970 million won this year, the first year.
Among the designated tasks, ‘Development of cod and tuna fish farming technology using open ocean deep cages’ will be carried out through collaborative research between the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute (KORDI) and the National Institute of Fisheries Science.
This project is a research project that proposes a groundbreaking fish farming model that can convert cage aquaculture facilities scattered in coastal bays into open ocean deep cage aquaculture.
In particular, it is attracting attention for its ability to utilize the underwater space of the open sea in a three-dimensional manner and for the development of mass aquaculture technology for high-quality fish species such as cod and tuna.
In addition, the ‘development of an automatic supply and automatic throwing device for conger eel trap bait’ is expected to contribute to securing the competitiveness of the fishing boat industry and improving productivity, as well as improving the quality of life for fishermen through automation of the trap fishing industry. The research institute is conducted by Professor Jeong Yong-gil of Gyeongsang National University.
From 1994 to last year, the fisheries-specific research and development project supported 375 projects worth 61.6 billion won, showing results such as 39 technology transfers, 160 domestic and foreign patent registrations, and 1,042 domestic and foreign paper presentations.
The Maritime and Fisheries Small and Medium Venture Business has so far provided 7.4 billion won to 52 companies and collected 280 million won in technology fees.

ko-news-notices-371-8372c75064.title: Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and Navy agree to strengthen national maritime power
ko-news-notices-371-8372c75064.text:
Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Navy agree to cooperate to strengthen national maritime power
2022-03-02
In order to strengthen national maritime power, the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Navy have decided to cooperate through establishing cooperation channels.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Navy will sign an ‘Agreement (MOU) for the formation of a maritime power development council’ at the Naval Headquarters of Gyeryongdae military complex in Daejeon at 3 p.m. on the 20th, with officials from both organizations, including Shin Pyung-sik, head of the Maritime Policy Division of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, and Seo Gyeong-jo, head of the Navy Policy and Public Relations Office, in attendance.
According to the MOU, it was decided to form a high-level council with the Vice Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Vice Chief of Staff of the Navy as the chairperson and up to six members from each agency to hold regular meetings every year and jointly discover and promote maritime-related cooperation.
In addition, a working council was formed with the Director of the Maritime Policy Division of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Director of the Navy's Policy and Public Relations Office as the chairpersons, and a meeting was decided to be held in the first half of each year, with the first meeting to be held on the 20th.
At the Maritime Power Development Council, various cooperation issues are discussed, including systematic management of marine territories such as Dokdo and the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), protection of national interests in the ocean, guaranteeing citizens' maritime activities, and cooperation in ocean development.
At the first working-level council meeting held on the 20th, various issues will be discussed, including ways to support the unmanned underwater vehicle (ROV, Remotely Operated Vehicle) being developed by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries for search and rescue activities in the event of a maritime disaster, a survey of the marine environment impact within the naval port, and the issue of naval personnel support for wintering units at the Sejong Base in Antarctica.
The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and the Navy have recently been working closely together by introducing an 'alternative military-service system for seafarers serving aboard ships' that provides exemption from military service to core sailors such as navigators and marine engineers, but also deploys them as personnel to transport strategic materials in times of emergency such as war.
It is expected that the conclusion of this MOU will establish a more solid cooperation channel between government and the military, thereby systematically managing maritime territory and enhancing national maritime power, while also providing an opportunity for early entry into the world's top five maritime powers.
Korea's maritime power is ranked 10th in the world, including 1st in shipbuilding, 5th in container throughput, 8th in shipping, and 15th in fisheries production. Naval power is also ranked 5th to 9th in the world, although there are some differences depending on evaluation factors.
In addition, on this day, the two organizations signed an ‘Agreement on Mutual Use of Comprehensive Marine Safety Information (MOU)’ and decided to jointly utilize location information of ships sailing off the coast of Korea.
As a result, it has become possible to monitor the operating status of ships in a wider sea area, from the existing 50 miles (about 90 km) to 150 miles (about 270 km, the distance from Seoul to Daegu), and to conduct rapid rescue and maritime control operations in the event of a maritime accident.
